From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@decisioning.ai>

Cc: procurement@decisioning.ai
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up from today's discovery — Decisioning inference constraints

Thanks for the call today, Grace — appreciate the time. Quick recap from our side and the top constraints we want to make sure are captured before the technical deep-dive: 

- Production workload: real-time decisioning for fraud scoring (single-call bot/decision per user event).
- Current observed P95 latency: ~450ms for our baseline LLM ensemble (two models), which spikes to >700ms during traffic bursts.
- Target SLOs: P95 <200ms; P99 ideally <400ms for 95% of traffic.
- Throughput: baseline 20 req/s per model, expected growth to 75 req/s over 6 months; short bursts up to 300 req/s across model replicas during batch scoring windows.
- Accuracy constraints: must preserve current model ensemble outputs — we cannot accept >2% delta on top-of-funnel scoring heuristics. Quantization must be validated against our eval set.
- Data/locality: customer data remains in our VPC — we need private deployment or a VPC-peering option (no cross-tenant data processing).

Next asks from Decisioning.ai: technical topology options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) with latency/throughput projections, an initial sizing, and what tradeoffs we can expect from batching + KV cache + quantization. Also would like a short mutual action plan we can share with procurement.

Happy to schedule the deep-dive next week — procurement looped in for commercial questions.

Regards,
Liam
Head of Platform Engineering
Decisioning.ai

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's discovery — Decisioning inference constraints

Thanks Liam — great summary. Below is a concise post-call technical synopsis and proposed next milestones so we can align internal and procurement stakeholders.

Recap of constraints (short):
- SLO target: P95 <200ms, burst tolerance to 300 RPS across the ensemble
- Throughput growth: 20 -> 75 RPS steady-state within 6 months
- Accuracy: <2% delta requirement on evaluation harness for any quantized/optimized variant
- Security: VPC-only data path or Private deployment; SOC2 + audit log requirements

Initial topology options (tradeoffs):
1) Redwood Dedicated (recommended starting point)
   - Predictable throughput via reserved GPU pool, autoscale policies for scale-up bursts, private networking (VPC peering).
   - Latency: with continuous batching tuned to sequence lengths and KV caching, P95 projection ~120-180ms for ensemble at steady 75 RPS.
   - Cost: higher fixed commit, but predictable unit economics — good if you need strict tail latency.

2) Hosted API + model-variant routing
   - Pros: fastest time-to-value and simpler procurement. Fallback to cheaper model variants possible.
   - Cons: harder to guarantee private data path; tail latency more variable under burst without capacity reservation.

3) Private (on-prem / customer VPC)
   - Pros: full control, meets your data locality ask.
   - Cons: longer lead time, integration tasks (KMS/HSM, audit log export), but most deterministic latency once onboarded.

Performance levers we propose to use (technical):
- KV cache for repeated prefix tokens in the ensemble to reduce compute for short context flows.
- Quantization profile: start with int8/q4xx experiment; strict evaluation on your eval set before rollout to ensure <2% delta.
- Continuous batching with latency-aware cutoffs (to avoid long tail amplification).
- Multi-variant routing: low-latency endpoint for 90% of traffic, cheaper fallbacks for non-critical batch windows.

Proposed next milestones (mutual action plan stub):
- Week 0: sign NDA + mutual action plan (procurement) — attached: mutual_action_plan.xlsx
- Week 1: technical deep-dive (1.5hr): topology sizing, perf targets, eval harness handoff
- Week 2-3: perf pilot (test harness + smoke runs) on a dedicated node group + quantization validation
- Week 4: rollout plan and procurement terms (commit sizing or Private onboarding)

Ben (cc) will outline a standard pilot commercial construct we typically use and the one-time onboarding items. Would you and procurement be available Tue or Wed next week for the deep-dive?

—Grace
